clue.text: The company of saints enshrined by poet

indicators.note: to be enshrined is to be held inside a shrine, so the poet's letters enclose the saints

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American poet
S is the abbreviation for saint, so SS stands for saints

explanation.surface: The heavenly host of saints is kept safe within a poet's verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saints' gives SS because S is the usual abbreviation for one saint; 'enshrined by' puts them inside the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band or group of people acting together, a synonym for a company in that sense.

clue.text: Caliper, twice beginning to perish, renovated by a bit of wire

indicators.note: the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement
the single letter is taken two times
the starting letter of the word perish

explanation.surface: A caliper, wearing out, is patched up with a scrap of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives P from perish, 'twice' doubles it, and 'renovated' rearranges CALIPER plus PP.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip is a small bent loop of wire for holding sheets together.

clue.text: Making a sudden movement springs onto mare

parts.note: spas are mineral springs
M is an abbreviation for mare in horse-breeding records

explanation.surface: A horse jumps up suddenly, springing onto a mare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is a link word; 'onto' puts the letters for mare after SPAS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an abrupt involuntary jerk or contraction of a muscle.

clue.text: Always on the outside, but not unknown

indicators.note: the letter for an unknown is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: externally means on the outer side
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone is perpetually outside yet somehow still familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes X, the unknown quantity in algebra, from EXTERNALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on forever, for all time, happens without end.

clue.text: Don't mention flat dope's concealed there

indicators.note: the letters of the words flat and dope's are disguised, hidden in a new order, which signals the rearrangement

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain letters here, with its S kept

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the flat: there's a stash of drugs hidden in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed there' asks for FLAT and DOPES to be rearranged; an unusual anagram signal, but the nine letters fit exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal something is to play it down or avoid stressing it, so not to mention it much.

clue.text: Try eating each vegetable

indicators.note: the word for an attempt swallows another word

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or go
all, as in a score of one all, means for each side

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to taste every vegetable on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' gives ALL as in a score of one all, meaning one for each side; 'eating' puts it inside the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb used in cooking.

clue.text: Entering battle, soldiers load

indicators.note: the soldiers go into the word for battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops going into combat carry their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts the Royal Engineers, the usual crossword soldiers, inside the battle; 'load' is the definition, a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo carried by a ship, train or lorry.

clue.text: Somebody turns up on the books, somebody who's essential

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for an important person is read upwards

parts.note: a VIP, very important person, is a somebody
OT, the Old Testament, the books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An important person shows up on the company's books, someone indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses VIP to PIV, set 'on' (above) OT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The pivot of a team is the central person on whom everything turns.

clue.text: Flushes in long conversation

indicators.note: the cleaning word is placed inside the word for yearn

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, so die means long
to scour a pipe is to flush it out with water

explanation.surface: Someone goes red in the face during a lengthy chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flushes' suggests blushing but means cleans out with water; 'long' is a verb, as in dying for something. 'in' puts the one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is serious spoken exchange, talk between people.

clue.text: Inclined to be fast, so they say

indicators.note: the word for a period of fasting is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone is disposed to go without food, or so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun for not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant means sloped or tilted, and also tended towards, as in leant towards an opinion.

clue.text: Job title — Reading, for instance

parts.note: a place is a post or position of employment
a title is a name given to something

explanation.surface: A job title is listed, then an example given, as if filling in a form.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, England; the capital R hides that behind the sense of reading a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is an English town, so its name is an example of what a gazetteer lists for a locality.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic supporters — they are in the forefront for match

indicators.note: only the front letter of each of the five words very, enthusiastic, supporters, they and are is taken

explanation.surface: The keenest fans are always at the front of the crowd for a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture but means the thing struck to make a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is a short wax match, named after the Roman goddess of the hearth.

clue.text: Gypsy not entirely an upright type

indicators.note: the word for a gypsy is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: Romany is the name of the Roma people and their language

explanation.surface: A traveller is described as being not quite a person of upright character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final Y. 'upright type' suggests an honest person but means printing type set straight rather than sloping italic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the ordinary upright typeface, as opposed to sloping italic.

clue.text: Leaves when it's time to go to bed

definitions.meaning: ..., in informal use, means departs in a hurry

definitions.text: when it's time to go to bed
definitions.meaning: the moment in a dormitory or barracks when the lamps must be switched off

explanation.definitionFit: To light out is slang for going off quickly, and the phrase is also the bedtime signal in schools or the army.

clue.text: Tall fee negotiated for promotional literature

indicators.note: the letters of tall fee are bargained over and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A high fee has been agreed for producing advertising material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges the letters of TALL FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed sheet handed out to advertise something is a typical piece of promotional material.

clue.text: When one is embraced by somebody, it can give rise to calumny

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the hug of the word for somebody

parts.note: a person is somebody
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Hugging someone can sometimes start a slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the Roman numeral I; 'is embraced by' puts it inside the word for somebody, after the word for when.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging statement, a slur on someone's character.

clue.text: As a help to people who are scared, a change of leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for frightened people is swapped for another

parts.note: cowards are timid, easily frightened people

explanation.surface: A cowed group might be helped by getting a new person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change of leader' replaces the C at the front of COWARDS with T.
explanation.definitionFit: Money given towards something is a contribution helping to pay for it.

clue.text: Exposed twisters perhaps expressed sorrow

parts.note: twisters (tornadoes) are an example of winds
wept means cried in grief

explanation.surface: Someone caught out in the open after the tornadoes cried.
explanation.definitionFit: A windswept place is open to the wind, unsheltered.

clue.text: Court had sinner trembling

indicators.note: shaking the letters of had sinner throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer was left shaking before the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' rearranges the letters of HAD SINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanhedrin was the supreme council and law tribunal of ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Sailor's daughter amazed

parts.note: Popeye is the cartoon sailor man who eats spinach

explanation.surface: A sailor's daughter is left astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with eyes wide open in astonishment is said to be bug-eyed, that is, amazed.

clue.text: Disagreement in the foreign fishing boat

indicators.note: the quarrel goes inside the foreign word

parts.note: der is German for the
a rift is a split or quarrel

explanation.surface: There is a quarrel aboard a foreign trawler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the foreign' is German's masculine article; 'in' puts the quarrel inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a boat that fishes with drift nets.

clue.text: Extortioner has gone astray in prison

parts.note: a dun is a persistent collector demanding payment of a debt

indicators.note: the word gone wanders off course, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A blackmailer who has gone off the rails ends up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A dun is an old word for someone pressing a debtor for money; 'astray' jumbles GONE to GEON after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell in a castle, a kind of jail.

clue.text: Edward remonstrated, not having accepted rising disgrace

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole sequence of letters is read upwards

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: the letter for acceptable is dropped from the word for remonstrated

parts.note: argued means protested or remonstrated
U is the label for upper-class, socially accepted usage

explanation.surface: Edward protested, refusing to accept a growing shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes U from ARGUED to give ARGED; ED plus ARGED is EDARGED, which 'rising' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to humiliate or dishonour them, bring them into disgrace.

clue.text: Youth employed to skin fish

parts.note: to strip is to peel off a covering
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A young lad is taken on at the fishmonger's to gut and skin the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man not yet fully grown, a lad.

clue.text: Completely lacking in grace

definitions.meaning: as in bored ..., meaning to an extreme degree
awkward, formal and unrelaxed in manner

explanation.definitionFit: Stiff intensifies as in scared stiff, and a stiff manner is rigid and awkward.

clue.text: Diminutive animal — gosh!

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigmy, variant of pygmy, is something very small of its kind.

clue.text: Black and brown fur

definitions.meaning: the pelt of a small Siberian marten, dark brown and highly prized

explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry sable is the colour black, and the same word names a marten whose dark brown coat is a luxury pelt.

clue.text: Beauty in the sound we hear

indicators.note: the ringing word is spoken, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: a bell is something that sounds when struck

explanation.surface: There is loveliness in the tones that reach our ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, often the most admired one present.

clue.text: It's seen in the Antarctic, in general

definitions.text: It's seen in the Antarctic, in general

indicators.note: the letters are visible inside the run of words antarctic, in general

explanation.surface: Something is commonly found at the South Pole.

explanation.definitionFit: Icing, the build-up of frost and ice on surfaces, is a common sight in polar regions.

clue.text: Wayfarer — flower is his joy

definitions.meaning: someone on a journey, especially on foot
the wild clematis is called by a name meaning the delight of a wanderer

explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is anyone on a journey, and traveller's joy is the British name for the wild clematis seen in hedgerows.

clue.text: By Jove! Liberal lacking commitment!

free means generous or liberal, as in free with money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with a capital suggests the British political party, but it just means generous.

clue.text: Old English noble at that time holding the capital of Gaul

indicators.note: the word for then wraps round the letter taken from Gaul

parts.note: then means at that time

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, of the word Gaul
